baselineFit.target: one-match MLS stat fit: goals ~2-3, shots ~26, SOT ~9, corners ~8, long-range SOT <=3

soccerStructure.target: soccer-like structure: width >=18, center+narrow <=35%, overload share >=25%, danger marking >=78%, shot corridor defenders >=1.2, empty-box shots <=35%, pattern touches >=2, real crosses >=5

tuningEfficiency.target: low-tweak debt: forced shots <=55%, final-third backpasses <=18, lateral flips <=90, direct-blocker passes <=70, broken rows <=10%

recommendations: Final-third recycling is still too common. Tighten attacker backpass vetoes and extend the carry-or-shoot window before resets are allowed.
Shape is still too central. Strengthen weak-side width anchors and reduce carrier-gravity pull on wide roles and midfield support.
Danger-zone attackers are still too often unmarked. Tighten goal-side marking assignments for box, cutback, and far-post runners without pulling the ball presser out of shape.
Too much of the final action still comes through central roles. Encourage wider occupation and more wing-led creation before the finish.
Corner volume is still unrealistically low. Review deflection, blocked-shot, and out-of-play logic so wider attacks can produce restarts naturally.
Some shots still lack second-wave support. Nudge nearby midfielders to arrive a little earlier into the edge-of-box support band.

Carrier zigzagging is still present. Reduce repeated lateral sign flips by holding the current carry lane longer and tightening the link between desired heading, facing heading, and actual movement heading.
Attackers are still lingering in the opponent box. Force dynamic box roles so extra attackers vacate, rotate, or resolve instead of standing in occupied central lanes.
